findings.text: `assert deferred.returncode == 0` (and the same shape at line 1119) cannot fail, because _stop returns 0 both when it emits a block and when it stays silent, so it counts as coverage without guarding the behaviour it names; only the stdout assertions at lines 1104 and 1120 can redden.

`assert deferred.stdout == ""` passes both when the acknowledgement defers the duty and when reapply_acknowledgements fails to defer it, because a failed deferral leaves the first stop's digest matching the unchanged blocking set and the stop is silent for the wrong reason, so this assertion survives the regression it claims to cover.

the repair's base and after arms re-run only tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py, while the done_when's arm over the five test files importing the changed module was not re-established at the repair's own base c6dba3af, so that part of the gate is inherited from the pre-repair round rather than measured against this change.
